requirement:
Each `AgentConfig` variant carries the corresponding settings from
`trust_but_verify::agent`. Serde uses the `backend` field to select `bedrock`,
`openai`, or `ollama` and reads the settings from the same object.

Choose [`BedrockConfig`](#habeas-req-requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.BedrockConfig),
[`OpenAiConfig`](#habeas-req-requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.OpenAiConfig), or
[`OllamaConfig`](#habeas-req-requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.OllamaConfig) for the selected backend.
With settings omitted, OpenAI uses `gpt-6.1-sol`, `https://api.openai.com/v1`,
and `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Ollama defaults to `http://localhost:11434`.

All three backend constructors start with an empty `options` map. Calling
`option(key, value)` inserts one inference setting. Calling it again with the
same key replaces its value and preserves the other settings. An `OptionValue` is
a `String`, `Boolean`, `Integer(i64)`, `Float(f64)`, `Array`, or `Map`. Arrays hold
option values and maps associate strings with option values. These serialize as
the corresponding untagged values. Backend calls reject nonfinite floats,
including those nested in an array or map.

`BedrockCredentials` contains `access_key_id` and `secret_access_key`, both
`SecretString`, and an optional `session_token` of the same type. Construct a
`SecretString` from `String` or `&str`. `expose_secret()` borrows its value.
Serialization preserves the string, while `Debug` prints `<redacted>`.
rationale:
The marked tests in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/config.rs` cover every obligation in `agent_config.settings`. There is one thin spot, covered in the `option` bullet.

- **`backend` selection and shared object.** `all_backends_preserve_nested_settings_and_credentials` deserializes a `bedrock`, `openai` and `ollama` object. Each carries its settings in the same object as `backend`. The test asserts that the serialized value equals the input and that a serialized copy equals the original. The same test also covers `Bedrock` credentials with a `session_token`. `configuration_debug_hides_credentials` additionally rejects an unknown setting.
- **Defaults.**
  - `option_defaults_and_credential_resolution_are_deterministic` asserts the OpenAI defaults `gpt-6.1-sol` and `https://api.openai.com/v1`.
  - The same test asserts the Ollama default `http://localhost:11434`.
  - `openai_uses_the_default_credential_variable` runs a child process with `OPENAI_API_KEY` set and asserts the default variable is read.
- **Empty options at construction.** `backend_builders_set_only_the_requested_fields` serializes freshly built Bedrock, OpenAI and Ollama configs. The output has no `options` entry for any of them.
- **`option` inserts and replaces.**
  - In the same test, the Bedrock chain `.option("a",1).option("b",true).option("a",2)` serializes to `{"a":2,"b":true}`. That shows replacement and preservation of other keys.
  - The OpenAI and Ollama builders each get a single `option` call, and the serialized value contains it.
  - Replacement for OpenAI and Ollama is not tested separately. Their `option` methods are the same single `self.options.insert(key, value)` call as Bedrock's, and the text does not distinguish backends here, so I do not count this as a gap.
- **`OptionValue` variants and untagged form.**
  - The nested round-trip covers string, integer, float, bool, array and map values.
  - `option_defaults_and_credential_resolution_are_deterministic` asserts that `1` deserializes to `Integer(1)` and `1.0` to `Float(1.0)`.
- **Nonfinite floats rejected, including nested.**
  - That test asserts that `OptionValue::validate` fails for a `Map` holding infinity.
  - It also asserts that `AgentConfig::Ollama(...).options_json()` fails for an `Array` holding NaN.
  - `options_json` validates every value for all three backends through one shared path.
- **`BedrockCredentials` and `SecretString`.**
  - `backend_builders_set_only_the_requested_fields` checks credentials serialization, round-trip and the optional `session_token`.
  - `configuration_debug_hides_credentials` checks construction from `String` and `&str`, `expose_secret()`, `Debug` printing `<redacted>`, and serialization that preserves the string.

I found no requirement-violating behavior that these tests would accept.
